LobbySettings.description: Island Battles game_settings for a lobby create request. Choose exactly one map: map_template_id, a default map from GET /map/templates, or map, a map file; settings without a map are refused. The map must be made for exactly the lobby's teams: player_amount equal to the team count, and castle team colours exactly 1 to that count, in team order, with 0 for neutral castles. turn_timeout_seconds sets how long each turn lasts, from 5 to 600 seconds, 30 when left out, or null for no limit. max_generations sets the most turns the game may last, a whole number from 50 to 1200, 300 when left out. turn_pace_milliseconds sets how long each turn of a real-time game lasts, a whole number of milliseconds from 500 to 5000, 1000 when left out; a game is real-time when a player on its roster plays by hand (bot kind manual), and then no turn times out. rated, false when left out, makes the game rated: it then starts only when every member is signed in and plays by hand or with a bot under one of their bot names, no two teams belong to one account, and every bot seat is a default bot level, each level once; the ready gate refuses anything else with game_requirement of type urn:island-battles:problem:rated-sign-in-required, urn:island-battles:problem:rated-bot-name-required, urn:island-battles:problem:rated-bot-name-gone, urn:island-battles:problem:rated-same-account or urn:island-battles:problem:rated-seat, and the game records each team's competitor. In a rated lobby a bot seat that isn't a default bot level, or a level already seated, is invalid_seat_settings, and turning rated on while such a seat is there is invalid_game_settings. An invalid choice fails lobby creation with invalid_game_settings, and its detail names each invalid field, such as game_settings.map.castles[0].x. The host can change them while the lobby waits, with the lobby's changeLobbySettings (PUT …/settings), which checks them as on create: send one team per colour of the new map. The start uses the map, turn timeout, game length, turn pace and rated set last, and checks them again.

map.description: Start on this map file. Give this or map_template_id, not both.

map_template_id.description: Start on this default map, a map_template_id from GET /map/templates. Give this or map, not both.

max_generations.description: The most turns the game may last, a whole number from 50 to 1200; 300 when left out. The turn that creates generation max_generations ends the game, if nothing has ended it before, and the team with the most castles wins.

rated.description: Whether the game is rated, false when left out. A rated lobby starts only when every member is signed in and plays by hand, with one of their bot names or with a registered bot, no two teams belong to one account, every bot seat is a default bot level, each level once, or a registered bot, each once, and the bots that play away have rated games left today. The game then records the competitor of each team, and its end changes their Elo ratings.

turn_pace_milliseconds.description: How long each turn lasts in a real-time game, in whole milliseconds from 500 to 5000; 1000 when left out. A game is real-time when a player on its roster plays by hand: each turn then ends this long after the previous one, and the server plays it with the commands that arrived, so a player who sent nothing passes. A game of bots only doesn't use it and waits for every player.

turn_timeout_seconds.description: How long each turn lasts, in whole seconds from 5 to 600, counted from when its generation was created; 30 when left out. null means no limit, for example while debugging a bot. When a turn's deadline passes before every player has completed it, each team with a player who hadn't loses, and the game ends. In a real-time game, see turn_pace_milliseconds, no turn times out; instead a player the server hasn't heard from for this long, or for one turn plus 5 seconds when that is longer, by the end of a turn has left the game and their team is out, and a game that no request reaches for this long after its open turn's end is abandoned: the team with the most castles wins. null turns both rules off.

castles.description: Each castle's position in the list is its castle ID in every game built from the map.

map_name.description: Name of the map, unique among default maps.

neutral_starting_soldier_amount.description: Soldiers in every castle, owned or neutral, that sets no starting_soldier_amount.

plane_size_x.description: Width of the plane, which is centred on the origin.

plane_size_y.description: Height of the plane, which is centred on the origin.

player_amount.description: Teams the map is made for, from 2 to 16, one player each. Castle team colours run from 1 to player_amount, and every one of them owns at least one castle.

castle_count.description: Castles on the map, team and neutral.

map_template_id.description: Choose the map by passing this ID as game_settings.map_template_id when creating a lobby.

team_count.description: Teams the map is made for, its player_amount. A lobby on this map has exactly this many teams, in team colour order.

MemberBot.description: The bot you choose for yourself. Send only the field of its kind: level for default, url for hosted, package_id for uploaded, and port, or none, for localhost; manual takes no other field. localhost, hosted and uploaded may also take name, one of your bot names. A localhost bot's port is from 1024 to 65535, 41414 when left out. A hosted bot's URL is https://, at most 2048 characters, without credentials, on port 443 or none, and names a host, not an IP address, whose addresses are all public: not loopback, private, link-local or unique-local. The server resolves it when you choose it, and again before it sends each turn. An uploaded bot is one of your ready packages in the lobby; if you replace or delete it, choose it again before getting ready.

competitor_id.description: For kind hosted only, instead of url and name: a bot name by its competitor_id: any registered bot with a URL, rated or not (GET /bots/registered), or one of your own bot names. It plays at the name's URL as it is at the start. Another account's bot plays away: in a rated lobby it is that bot that plays for your team, your own hand play isn't in the game, and the daily caps and the pause apply to it. One of your own plays as if you named it. In a lobby that isn't rated it rates nothing.

kind.description: localhost: your own bot, which island-battles-bot serve runs on your machine and your game client relays each turn to. default: a default bot of GET /bots/defaults, which the backend plays. hosted: your own bot server at url, which the server sends each turn to. uploaded: your own bot package in this lobby, package_id, which the server runs. manual: you play by hand in the 3D client; no bot plays for you. hosted and uploaded are offered only when GET /bots/defaults says server_bots.

level.description: For kind default only: a level that GET /bots/defaults lists.

name.description: For kinds localhost, hosted and uploaded only: one of the bot names of your account (GET /account), compared without regard to case, that the bot plays as. Only a signed-in player has bot names. A rated lobby takes a bot only as a hosted bot under a bot name, which plays at the name's URL, and records the game under the name. Elsewhere the name changes nothing, except that a hosted bot without a url plays at its name's URL.

package_id.description: For kind uploaded only: a package of yours in this lobby, from GET /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages.

port.description: For kind localhost only: the port on 127.0.0.1 where your bot serves (island-battles-bot serve --port N), where your game client delivers each turn. 41414 when absent.

url.description: For kind hosted only: where the server POSTs each TurnDelivery. https:// on port 443, without credentials, on a host name (not an IP address) whose addresses are all public. Required unless the bot has a name or a competitor_id, which then plays at its own URL (GET /account). In a rated lobby a named hosted bot always plays at its name's URL, and url is ignored.

MemberSettings.description: Island Battles member_settings for setLobbyMemberSettings: the bot that plays for you. {"bot": {"kind": "manual"}} is you, playing by hand in the 3D client: no bot plays or relays for you, and your client sends your commands with POST /generation/commands. {"bot": {"kind": "localhost"}} is your own bot, which island-battles-bot serve runs on your machine and your game client relays each turn to, on port 41414 or on the port you add, {"bot": {"kind": "localhost", "port": 41415}}, and {"bot": {"kind": "default", "level": N}} a default bot of a level that GET /bots/defaults lists, which the backend plays itself. When GET /bots/defaults says server_bots, also {"bot": {"kind": "hosted", "url": "https://…"}}, your own bot server at a public URL, or {"bot": {"kind": "uploaded", "package_id": "…"}}, one of your bot packages in the lobby; the server plays both, without your game client. A localhost, hosted or uploaded bot may add "name", one of the bot names of your account (GET /account), compared without regard to case: {"bot": {"kind": "localhost", "name": "Kraken"}}. A name that isn't one of yours, or any name from a guest, is invalid_member_settings; it is accepted in every lobby, but only a rated lobby, where a bot needs one, records the game under it. Anything else is invalid_member_settings. You choose a bot before getting ready, and can change it while the lobby waits: getting ready without one is refused with game_requirement of type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-not-chosen, and an uploaded bot that is no longer a ready package of yours in the lobby, replaced, deleted or someone else's, with type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-package-gone. The start checks every roster player and bot seat the same way. It then initializes one playable generation, which waits for every frozen roster player to complete their turn, and copies each roster player's bot, and each bot seat's, which GenerationState.bot reports from then on.

fields.description: The form fields to send before the file, unchanged.

url.description: POST a multipart/form-data body here: every field of fields, then the zip as the last field, named file.

team_ids.description: The teams the error is about. For empty_teams, the teams that still need a player, in team order.

type.description: For game_requirement, the game's own problem type, a URI that the game documents, such as one meaning a player has yet to choose something in the game's API. Absent for every other code.

after.description: The competitor's rating after the game, a decimal: show it rounded.

before.description: The competitor's rating before the game, a decimal: show it rounded.

kind.description: bot: a bot name that an account registered. manual: an account's hand play. house: a default bot level.

name.description: The name the competitor is shown by: a bot's name, such as Kraken, the account's display name for its hand play, or Bot (level N) for a house bot.

owner.description: The display name of the account that the bot name belongs to, for kind bot only.

name.description: The bot's name: 3 to 24 characters after trimming, of letters, digits, spaces, - and _, not starting with Bot (level. It is unique across all accounts without regard to case.

url.description: The bot's hosted bot URL, where the server sends it each turn in a rated lobby: https:// on port 443, without credentials, on a host name (not an IP address) whose addresses are all public, as a hosted bot's. It is public, in GET /bots/registered, so that others can play against it.

$schema.description: A URL to the JSON Schema for this object.

complete.description: Seals your turn after this batch. Defaults to true.

logs.description: Game log lines written since your previous batch for this generation, appended in order after the lines already stored. At most 100 lines per player per generation, each of at most 500 characters; a batch that would break either limit is rejected whole with 422 and problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-log-limit.

memory.description: Your bot's memory, the BotTurnResult.memory it returned: any JSON object of at most 64 KiB as compact JSON. Only the batch with complete true saves it, replacing your previous memory, and an absent or null memory clears it; other batches ignore it. GenerationState.memory returns it. Larger memory is rejected whole with 422 and problem type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-memory-too-large.

request_id.description: Identifies this batch. Retry a lost request with the same UUID and body; use a new UUID for every new batch.

competitor_id.description: Choose it by this ID: a member's {"kind": "hosted", "competitor_id": "…"} or a seat's {"bot_competitor_id": "…"}.

name.description: The bot's registered name, such as Kraken.

owner.description: The display name of the account that owns it, as in "Kraken, by Dana".

rated.description: Whether it has played a rated game, and so is on the leaderboard. An unrated bot can be chosen too.

rating.description: Its Elo rating, rounded, once it is rated; null before its first rated game.

url.description: Its hosted bot's URL, where the server plays it.

$schema.description: A URL to the JSON Schema for this object.

bots.description: The page's bots: rated ones first, by rating, highest first, then unrated ones, each by name.

total.description: How many registered bots match the search.

display_name.description: The seat's name in the lobby, such as "Localhost bot (port 41415)".

player_id.description: The seat's player ID on the roster, which GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/turn-delivery?player_id= takes.

port.description: The port on 127.0.0.1 where your client delivers the seat's turns.

soldier_amount.description: Soldiers to send; counts against soldiers already reserved by your team this turn.

url.description: The bot's hosted bot URL, where the server sends it each turn in a rated lobby: https:// on port 443, without credentials, on a host name (not an IP address) whose addresses are all public, as a hosted bot's. It is public, in GET /bots/registered, so that others can play against it.

clash_radius.description: Enemies clash when their centers are within the larger of their radii.

id.description: Soldier group ID, never reassigned within a game.

upgrades.description: Every upgrade type's level, copied from the origin castle when the group left.

TurnDelivery.description: One turn delivered to a bot that runs outside the backend, such as the player's own bot server: the BotTurn to play, and where and with which submit token to submit the answer. A bot server answers the delivery with 202 at once and submits its BotTurnResult itself as one completing batch.

$schema.description: A URL to the JSON Schema for this object.

deadline_at.description: When the turn ends, the BotTurn's turn_deadline_at, or null when turns have no time limit. An answer should be submitted before it: in a real-time game a later one joins the turn open when it arrives, but this submit token expires 30 seconds after deadline_at, so that is the latest an answer can come.

token.description: The submit token, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. It lets the bearer submit this player's turn of this generation and nothing else, and expires at the turn's deadline plus 30 seconds, or 24 hours after the generation when turns have no time limit. Keep it secret until the turn is over.

url.description: Where to submit the answer: POST /generation/commands on the game's server, as an absolute URL.

levels.description: Every level from 1 to max_level, in order.

max_level.description: The highest level. Every castle starts at level 1.

castle_id.description: Castle your team owns. It pays the level's soldier_cost from GET /game/upgrades.

upgrade_type.description: The type to raise by one level. Several upgrades of a castle in one turn each buy the next level.

soldier_cost.description: Soldiers the castle pays to reach this level from the level below. Level 1 is free.

value.description: The level's effect, in the unit its type's description names.

UpgradeType.description: A castle upgrade. GET /game/upgrades lists each type's levels and costs.

state.description: The final generation, with its outcome.

$schema.description: A URL to the JSON Schema for this object.

channel.description: The lobby's watch channel, watch:island-battles:<lobby_id>, which receives WatchGenerationEvent after each turn and WatchGameEndedEvent after the last one.

departures.description: The teams that have resigned or left this real-time game so far, as in GenerationState.

lobby_round.description: The lobby round that the game plays. A lobby plays one game per round, and the /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id} routes serve its newest game: compare this with the lobby snapshot's lobby.round to tell whether the game is the one the lobby started last.

outcome.description: How the game ended. Absent while the game runs.

teams.description: The teams that play, with their lobby names and the display names their players had at the start.

turn_deadline_at.description: When this generation's turn ends, as GenerationState.turn_deadline_at describes. Null when turns have no time limit, and once the game has ended. Watchers never apply a deadline themselves.

turn_pace_milliseconds.description: The game's turn pace in milliseconds when the game is real-time, as in GenerationState; null when the game waits for every player.

DemoToken.description: A demo token, which starts with ibdt1., in the token query parameter, as the link GameEndedDelivery.demo.url carries it; Authorization: Bearer ibdt1.… works too. It authorizes GET /game/{id}/demo of its one game, as its one roster player sees it, and nothing else, until GameEndedDelivery.demo.expires_at, when game retention deletes the game.
DemoToken.name: token

LobbyBearer.description: Bearer credential of a session, issued by POST /lobby/v1/sessions to a guest or by POST /lobby/v1/sessions/google to a signed-in player. This is distinct from a Centrifugo connection JWT.

PlayerToken.description: A player token for the island-battles game, from POST /lobby/v1/player-tokens with game_key island-battles: a JWT signed with EdDSA that the game verifies with the lobby's public keys, GET /lobby/v1/jwks.json, without reading the lobby. It lasts at most 15 minutes, until its expires_at; get a new one before then, at about 80 % of its life, and once more when a request answers 401. The guest credential of POST /lobby/v1/sessions is refused here: a missing, expired or invalid token is 401.

SubmitToken.description: A submit token from a TurnDelivery, submit.token, which starts with ibst1. It authorizes POST /generation/commands for one player's turn of one generation of one game, until the turn's deadline plus 30 seconds, or 24 hours after the generation when turns have no time limit. In a real-time game the deadline comes one turn pace after the previous turn's, and a batch that comes later joins the open turn however late it is, so for a bot that answers with a submit token these 30 seconds are the effective limit: a later answer is refused with 401.

UploadToken.description: An upload token from POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages/upload-token, which starts with ibut1. It stands for its player in POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages and its complete, for that lobby only, for 15 minutes. Its payload, the base64url JSON between its two dots, names the lobby as lobby_id, which the command line reads.

info.description: Operations a player client calls during a started game. After every turn, each roster player's Centrifugo channel `player:{player_id}` receives a `GenerationEvent`, except after the turn that ends the game, which pushes a `GameEndedEvent` with the final generation and its outcome instead. Clients reconcile with the generation read after subscribing or reconnecting; HTTP state is authoritative, and its `outcome` is set once the game has ended. A turn times out at its `turn_deadline_at`; the server runs no timers, so a client waiting for other players calls `POST /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/deadline` about a second after it. `MapTemplate` is the map file format, which `POST /map/create` accepts. `LobbySettings` is the `game_settings` object of an Island Battles lobby create request; `GET /map/templates` lists the default maps it can choose. `GET /game/upgrades` lists what each castle upgrade level costs, and `GET /bots/defaults` the default bots that the backend plays. Before getting ready in a lobby, every member chooses their bot in their lobby member settings with the lobby's `setLobbyMemberSettings`: `{"bot": {"kind": "manual"}}`, a person who plays by hand in the 3D client, `{"bot": {"kind": "localhost"}}`, their own bot, whose turns their client relays, or `{"bot": {"kind": "default", "level": N}}`, a default bot level; `GenerationState.bot` reports it during the game. `Demo` is the demo file format, which `GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/demo` returns and the demo viewer at `/game/demo-viewer/` opens. People outside the roster watch a game with its lobby's join code (`POST /lobby/v1/watches`): the lobby's watch channel `watch:island-battles:{lobby_id}` receives a `WatchGenerationEvent` after every turn and a `WatchGameEndedEvent` after the last, in the same push as the players' events, and `GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/watch`, `/watch/demo` and `/watch/logs` are their reads. `BotTurn` and `BotTurnResult` are the stateless bot contract: a bot gets a `BotTurn` each turn and answers with a `BotTurnResult`, which is sent as one completing batch. A localhost bot gets its turns as a `TurnDelivery` from `GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/turn-delivery`, which its player's client posts to it, and submits its answer itself with the delivery's one-turn submit token. When the game ends, every bot that runs outside the backend gets a `GameEndedDelivery`, with the outcome and a self-contained link to the game's demo, `GET /game/{id}/demo?token=ibdt1.…`: the server sends it to hosted and uploaded bots, and a localhost bot's client relays it from `GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/game-ended-delivery`. Any member of a lobby can upload a bot package, the zip that the SDKs' `package` command builds, to the lobby: `POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages` presigns the upload, the zip goes straight to storage, and `POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages/{package_id}/complete` checks it. The command line uploads with an upload token from `POST /game/lobbies/{lobby_id}/bot-packages/upload-token` instead of a session.
info.title: Island Battles Player API

delete.description: Requires the player token of a signed-in player; a guest's token is 403 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:sign-in-required. Deletes every competitor of the account, its bot names and its hand play with their ratings, and the game's record of the account, unless the account is hidden from the leaderboard: then the game keeps its record, with its display name, so that it stays hidden, with its new hand play and bot names, when it plays again. Call it before the lobby's DELETE /lobby/v1/account, so the game's part is gone first. Deleting an account the game doesn't know is 204 too.
delete.summary: Delete your account's part of the game

get.description: Requires the player token of a signed-in player, which names their account; a guest's token is 403 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:sign-in-required. Every call stores the account the first time the game sees it, with its hand play, and the display name of the token whenever it changed, so a rename in the lobby reaches the game with the next player token. A competitor is what gets a rating: each bot name an account registers, and the account's hand play, shown under its display name. Each starts at a rating of 1500. Returns the account's ID and display name, max_bot_names (5), its hand play and its bot names, oldest first, each bot name with its hosted bot's url, which is null for a name registered before names had URLs.
get.summary: Read your account: your hand play and your bot names

post.description: Requires the player token of a signed-in player, which names their account; a guest's token is 403 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:sign-in-required. Every call stores the account the first time the game sees it, with its hand play, and the display name of the token whenever it changed, so a rename in the lobby reaches the game with the next player token. Registers a bot name, a competitor at a rating of 1500, with the URL of the hosted bot that plays it, and returns it. A name is 3 to 24 characters after trimming, of letters, digits, spaces, - and _, and can't start with Bot (level, otherwise 422. The url is required and must pass a hosted bot's check (https:// on port 443, without credentials, on a host name whose addresses are all public), otherwise 422. In a rated lobby the name plays as a hosted bot at this URL. GET /bots/registered lists the name with its URL at once, so that others can play against it, and once it has played a rated game the leaderboard lists it too. Names are unique across all accounts without regard to case: a taken name is 409 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-name-taken. An account has at most 5 bot names: a sixth is 409 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-name-limit. A name can't be renamed: delete it and register another.
post.summary: Register a bot name in your account, with its hosted bot's URL

delete.description: Requires the player token of a signed-in player, which names their account; a guest's token is 403 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:sign-in-required. Every call stores the account the first time the game sees it, with its hand play, and the display name of the token whenever it changed, so a rename in the lobby reaches the game with the next player token. Deletes the bot name with its rating. The name is free at once, and registering it again makes a new competitor at 1500. Another account's bot name, or an unknown one, is 404.
delete.summary: Delete one of your bot names

put.description: Requires the player token of a signed-in player, which names their account; a guest's token is 403 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:sign-in-required. Every call stores the account the first time the game sees it, with its hand play, and the display name of the token whenever it changed, so a rename in the lobby reaches the game with the next player token. Sets the bot name's url, which must pass a hosted bot's check, otherwise 422, and returns the bot name. It keeps its rating. A rated game plays the URL that the name had when the game started. A listed name's new URL shows on the leaderboard within a minute. A name registered before names had URLs needs one before it can play in a rated lobby. Another account's bot name, or an unknown one, is 404.
put.summary: Change the hosted bot URL of one of your bot names

delete.description: Requires the player token of a signed-in player, which names their account; a guest's token is 403 with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:sign-in-required. Every call stores the account the first time the game sees it, with its hand play, and the display name of the token whenever it changed, so a rename in the lobby reaches the game with the next player token. A bot name plays away when it sits in a bot seat, or when a member of another account chose it, in a rated lobby that someone else opened. One that misses a turn there loses the game, as any rated game, and is paused: it plays away in no rated game until its owner resumes it here. Your own games with it are unaffected. Clears the bot name's away_paused and answers 200 with the bot name; resuming a name that isn't paused changes nothing. Another account's bot name, your hand play, or an unknown one is 404.
delete.summary: Let one of your bot names play away again after it missed a turn

get.description: Lists the default bots in level order, each with its level, a name and a description of how it plays. Higher levels play better. The backend plays a default bot itself, with no client: it plays each turn as soon as the generation is created, so it never misses a turn's deadline. A game in which only default bots are left plays on by itself, and each game request continues it for a few seconds. The list is static and needs no authentication. server_bots says whether the server also offers hosted and uploaded bots, which it plays without a player's tab, in member settings and bot seats.
get.summary: List the default bots that the backend plays, and whether it offers hosted and uploaded bots.

get.description: Public: it needs no credential. It lists every registered bot name that has a hosted bot URL, across all accounts, with its owner's display name and its URL, whether or not it has played a rated game. Anyone may choose one by its competitor_id: for their own team, as a member's {"kind": "hosted", "competitor_id": "…"}, or as a seat, {"bot_competitor_id": "…"}, and the server plays it at its URL, without its owner joining. A deleted bot name, one without a URL, and the bots of an account that the admin hid aren't listed. search keeps only the bots whose name or owner's display name holds it, without regard to case. The order is rated bots first, by rating, highest first, then unrated bots by name; limit (1 to 100, default 50) and offset (default 0) page through it, and total counts the bots that match.

get.description: Uploaded bots run in the server's bot runners, whose compute has a monthly budget, so that they stay inside Lambda's free tier. Once the runners have used it this month (UTC), a lobby whose start roster has an uploaded bot, a member's or a bot seat's, can't start until the first of the next month: the start fails with the lobby's game_requirement of type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-compute-spent, and the bot pickers grey out uploaded bots with the same sentence. Games already running go on, and games with only localhost, hosted and default bots are unaffected. The runners' compute is read from CloudWatch at most once per 10 minutes and kept in between, so this needs no authentication. A server that doesn't measure it, such as a local one, reports 0 and available. 503 when the compute can't be read.
get.summary: Say whether games with uploaded bots may start this month.

post.description: Requires a place on the game's frozen roster; the lobby is not consulted. The server runs no timers, so a turn ends when a request finds its deadline, GenerationState.turn_deadline_at, passed. Every game request does that first, and a client that is waiting for the turn to end calls this once the deadline has passed. Before the deadline, and for a game that has ended or has no turn timeout, it changes nothing. In a real-time game (GenerationState.turn_pace_milliseconds isn't null, because a player plays by hand) the deadline, turn_deadline_at, comes one turn pace after the previous turn's deadline, but at least half a pace after the request that played that turn, and this plays the turn with the commands that arrived: the batches of players who haven't completed it, complete false included, are played, a player who sent nothing passes, and nobody loses for passing. The next generation is pushed as after any turn. Calling it again changes nothing until the next turn's deadline. A real-time game can also end without a conquest. A team leaves when its player resigns (POST /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/resign), or when the server hasn't heard from its player for the lobby's turn_timeout_seconds, or for one turn pace plus 5 seconds when that is longer, by the end of a turn: the turn that ends then takes the team out. Every game request made as a player, with a player token or a submit token, also one that is refused, counts as hearing from them, and a default bot is always heard. A team that leaves has its castles turn neutral, keeping their soldiers, and its soldier groups removed, and GenerationState.departures lists it; with two teams the other team wins. When no request has reached a real-time game for turn_timeout_seconds after its open turn's end, the next game request, whoever makes it, or the lobby's reopen, ends it on the open generation with reason abandoned: among the teams still in it the team with the most castles wins, and equal counts are a draw. With turn_timeout_seconds null nobody leaves by silence and no game is abandoned. In a game that waits for every player, after the deadline every team with a player who hasn't completed the turn loses, the game ends with reason turn_timeout, and among the other teams still standing the team with the most castles wins; equal counts, or no team left, are a draw. The open generation stays the final one, game.ended is pushed to every roster player, and later commands conflict (409) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-ended. Calling it again is safe and ends the game once. Returns your current state, as GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/generation does. A lobby can play several games, one per round (lobby.round, raised by POST /lobby/v1/games/island-battles/lobbies/{lobby_id}/reopen once a game has ended); this route serves the lobby's newest game and its frozen roster, and an older game can't be reached once the next one starts.
post.summary: End the current turn once its deadline has passed, for a roster player

get.description: Requires a place on the game's frozen roster; the lobby is not consulted. Returns the game as a demo file, the Demo schema, as an attachment named island-battles-game-<game_id>-generation-<n>.json, where n is the number of generations played. Any roster player can save a demo at any time: one saved during the game holds the generations played so far and a null outcome. Each frame's game log lines follow the rule of GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/logs when the demo is saved: while the game runs only your own team's lines, once it has ended every team's. The demo viewer at /game/demo-viewer/ opens the file without the lobby, a session or the game. The body is streamed, and a long game with full logs takes tens of megabytes, so it is packed with gzip (Content-Encoding: gzip) when Accept-Encoding allows it. post.description: Requires a player token of a player on the game's frozen roster (PlayerToken), or a submit token: Authorization: Bearer ibst1.… from GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/turn-delivery stands for its player for the batch of its game and generation only, and anything else (another game or generation, an expired or altered token, a player no longer on the roster) is 401. Either way the lobby is not consulted, and the rules below are the same. Players send send_soldier_group, upgrade_castle and burst_castle commands for castles their team owns; other command types are forbidden (403). upgrade_castle buys the next level of one upgrade type and pays that level's soldier_cost, listed by GET /game/upgrades, from the castle's soldiers. A castle may be upgraded several times in one turn, and each upgrade buys the next level. Every generation, each castle a team owns produces its generation_amount value of soldiers. burst_castle orders a burst of 1 up to the castle's burst_potential value, counting the turn's upgrades (every upgrade of its batch, before or after it, and of earlier batches; a batch's bursts are checked after its other commands): the very next generation adds it to the castle on top of its production and makes it the castle's burst_debt. Each later generation's production repays the debt first, and only what is left over grows the castle. A castle with burst_debt can't burst, nor can a castle burst twice in one turn; a capture clears the debt. Every command is checked against the generation and every command already accepted this turn, including your own earlier batches, so an accepted command cannot fail when the turn runs. An invalid command rejects the whole batch, and nothing of it is stored. Malformed parameters are 422. Rejections that clients tell apart carry a problem type: a castle that is not in the generation is 422 urn:island-battles:problem:castle-not-found, an unknown upgrade_type is 422 urn:island-battles:problem:unknown-upgrade-type, a castle your team does not own is 403 urn:island-battles:problem:castle-not-owned, an upgrade past its type's max_level, counting this turn's upgrades, is 409 urn:island-battles:problem:upgrade-max-level, soldiers or an upgrade cost beyond what the castle has left after this turn's reservations is 409 urn:island-battles:problem:insufficient-soldiers, a burst of a castle with burst_debt or a burst accepted this turn is 409 urn:island-battles:problem:burst-unavailable, and a burst above the castle's burst potential is 409 urn:island-battles:problem:burst-above-potential. A castle may spend all its soldiers. Complete defaults to true; an empty batch can complete a turn. The last frozen roster completion advances exactly once. The game ends after the turn that leaves one team with castles or soldier groups, a draw when the last teams are eliminated in the same turn, or after the turn that creates the game's last generation, game_settings.max_generations (300 when the lobby sets none), where the team with the most castles wins. That turn's generation is the last, its state carries the outcome, and every later command conflicts (409) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-ended. In a game that waits for every player, a turn also ends the game when its deadline, GenerationState.turn_deadline_at, passes before every roster player completed it: each team with a player who hadn't loses (outcome reason turn_timeout), the open generation stays the last, and a batch for it after the deadline conflicts with the same problem type. In a real-time game (GenerationState.turn_pace_milliseconds isn't null) a turn ends at its deadline, turn_deadline_at, one turn pace after the previous turn's deadline (the first one pace after the start), but at least half a pace after the request that played the previous turn: the request that finds it passed plays the turn with the commands that arrived, as if every player had completed it. A batch that arrives after the turn it names has played is late, and joins the turn open when it arrives instead, however many turns late it is: it is checked against the open generation and the commands already accepted in it, as any batch is, and refused for the usual reasons when it no longer fits; with complete true it completes your open turn and saves its memory, and its game log lines stay with the turn it names. The answer is the open turn's state. An answer that then comes in time for that open turn conflicts (409) with the detail player turn is already complete. A submit token expires 30 seconds after its turn's deadline, which limits how late a bot that answers with one can be. A late batch that arrives once you have completed the open turn, or that names no generation of this game, conflicts (409) as a stale generation, with a detail that names the pace. A real-time game can also end without a conquest. A team leaves when its player resigns (POST /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/resign), or when the server hasn't heard from its player for the lobby's turn_timeout_seconds, or for one turn pace plus 5 seconds when that is longer, by the end of a turn: the turn that ends then takes the team out. Every game request made as a player, with a player token or a submit token, also one that is refused, counts as hearing from them, and a default bot is always heard. A team that leaves has its castles turn neutral, keeping their soldiers, and its soldier groups removed, and GenerationState.departures lists it; with two teams the other team wins. When no request has reached a real-time game for turn_timeout_seconds after its open turn's end, the next game request, whoever makes it, or the lobby's reopen, ends it on the open generation with reason abandoned: among the teams still in it the team with the most castles wins, and equal counts are a draw. With turn_timeout_seconds null nobody leaves by silence and no game is abandoned. A batch of a player whose team resigned or left conflicts (409) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:team-out. Otherwise a new batch for a generation that is no longer current, in either kind of game, conflicts (409) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:stale-generation. Retry the same request UUID and payload safely, also after the game ended or the turn played: a request is applied at most once, in whichever turn it joined, and its retries answer your current state; changed payloads and stale new requests conflict. A batch may also carry game log lines, which are stored in order with the generation and read with GET /game/from-lobby/{lobby_id}/logs. A player has at most 100 lines per generation, each of at most 500 characters; a batch over either limit is rejected whole (422) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:game-log-limit. A batch may also carry the memory of the player's bot, any JSON object of at most 64 KiB as compact JSON. The batch with complete true saves it, replacing the player's previous memory, and an absent or null memory clears it; other batches ignore it. GenerationState.memory returns the memory sent with the player's latest completed turn, and the retry hash covers it. Larger memory is rejected whole (422) with problem type urn:island-battles:problem:bot-memory-too-large.
